source.quote: For the full year, we delivered $671 million of adjusted EBITDA, in line with our upwardly revised target of $650 million to $700 million and well above our original goal of $600 million to $650 million.
Lastly, in 2025, we generated $724 million of adjusted free cash flow compared to our original guidance of $650 million and revised guidance midyear of $750 million.

guide.quote: FTAI continues to expect 2025 Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $1.1 to $1.15 billion from its reportable segments, comprised of approximately $500 million from Aviation.

source.quote: Consistent with our view, we reaffirm our 2026 total business segment EBITDA outlook of $1.625 billion, comprised of $1.05 billion from aerospace products and $575 million from aviation leasing supported by growing and accelerating demand across our proprietary aerospace offerings.

As a reminder, 2026 Aerospace Products adjusted EBITDA guidance is $1.05 billion and 2026 Aviation Leasing guidance of $475 million. 2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.3 billion, comprised of $1.4 billion from Aerospace Products, $450 million-$750 million from FTAI Power, and $450 million from Aviation Leasing.
Net debt to run rate adjusted EBITDA was 2.2 times, down from 2.6 times at the end of the second quarter and below our target range of 2.5-3.0 times.
Adjusted EBITDA was $282.4 million, up 57% year-over-year at an EBITDA margin of 31%, in line with our guidance of 30%.
FTAI continues to expect 2025 Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $1.1 to $1.15 billion from its reportable segments, comprised of approximately $500 million from Aviation.
Additionally, FTAI is increasing its 2026 Adjusted EBITDA from its reportable segments from its previously projected $1.25 billion to be approximately $1.4 billion.

Introduced Business Segment 2027 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.3 billion, comprised of $1.4 billion from Aerospace Products, $450 million from FTAI Power and $450 million from Aviation Leasing (1)(2).

Reaffirmed 2026 Aerospace Products Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1,050 million and updated 2026 Aviation Leasing guidance from $575 million to $475 million reflecting our continued shift to an asset-light business model (1)(2). “FTAI delivered another strong quarter, led by record Aerospace Products performance and a landmark customer contract for FTAI Power," said Joe Adams, Chairman and CEO.
